messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#784] use of pipe() for input
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for your interest. I sure need to give this more thought but my first comment is that this wouldn't be a good fit with the rmr design which aims to be a tight pure r abstraction - forgive the mouthful. Allowing mixed Perl r programming is beyond what we were trying to do and seems pretty hard to squeeze into the current architecture. I don't see this happening.  Looking at  your example, compression is taken care of transparently by Hadoop and column selection will be part of a hcat input format which we hope to support in the future.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: use of pipe() for input
messages.body_plain: What I was thinking of was processing where the raw data in HDFS is a mess -- awkward format, missing fields and lots of stuff I don't need to include for my computation. In Hadoop Streaming the first job of the mapper script will be to filter this down to something usable by the reducer. In plain R, too, I often have this situation and I'd rather not use R's string processing and regex functions, because pipe() is much simpler. It means I can push the parsing work outside of R, so all R sees is a clean n-column feed.

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#787] Re: use of pipe() for input
messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#787] Re: use of pipe() for input
messages.body_plain:
So the point is not that R can't do what you need, just that you like to do it in multiple languages. The appropriate tool for that is hadoop streaming. Rmr is to write in R, not to replace streaming. I am afraid executing general pipelines in a distributed fashion is out of  scope. I know of at least one data scientist that has the same preference and he uses unvarnished streaming. Another alternative is to use streaming for preprocessing, write out the results to HDFS and then read those into rmr.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: topicmodels Document Term Matrix object issues
messages.body_plain:
Ok, this is a long shot. If this turns out to be more of a topicmodels issue, I will ask its developer instead.

I have two sets of tweets that I have chosen from two different twitter accounts on purpose. I want to run an LDA topic model on each set of tweets.

When I run the following code to model all the tweets

library(tm)
library(topicmodels)

testdf=data.frame(text=c("Fast Wagon vs Slow Sports Car - With Chris Harris - TUNED:","Porsche claiming 0-100mph for 991 GT3 is 7.5sec. That's quite fast.",
                        "New Aston V12 Vantage S v old V12V asks interesting question: more power, dynamics and paddles, or less power and a stick? I might go stick",
 "And Porsche insists that the car is faster as1640kg hybrid than it would be as 1200kg minus batteries because of 4wd/clever chassis",
 "I love my job. Giggling with Walter as he oversteers GT3 RS 4.0 in the wet.",
 "R8 V10 Plus v GTR by Litchfield v 911 Turbo S on @DRIVE . Think you'll like this one.",
 "One comment on 991 Turbo - width. For me, the car should be a wieldy package. Happy on smaller roads. 997 just about does that, 991 too big?",
 "Cloudera brings open source search to big data in Hadoop. Attend the WEBINAR to learn more",
 "Cloudera Search: Apache Solr-based, Google-style  search for Hadoop, speed access to #BigData",
 "The inspiration for the name Hadoop lives in @cutting's sock drawer.",
 "Planned maintenance is the single largest cause of Hadoop downtime. But not for Cloudera customers!"),
  topic=c(1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,2,2))

corp = Corpus(VectorSource(testdf$text))
corp = tm_map(corp, tolower)
corp = tm_map(corp, stripWhitespace)
corp = tm_map(corp, removePunctuation)
corp = tm_map(corp, removeNumbers)
corp = tm_map(corp, removeWords, stopwords('english'))
corp.DTM = DocumentTermMatrix(corp)
topic_model = LDA(corp.DTM,k=2)
n_results = 2
terms = terms(topic_model, n_results)

print(terms)

I get

> source("rmr_test.R")
     Topic 1  Topic 2
[1,] "car"    "hadoop"
[2,] "search" "power"

When I separately ran it for the two groups, I got:

> source("rmr_test_1.R")
     Topic 1 Topic 2
[1,] "car"   "car"
[2,] "fast"  "porsche"
> source("rmr_test_2.R")
     Topic 1    Topic 2
[1,] "hadoop"   "hadoop"
[2,] "cloudera" "search"

Now, I want to do topic models for tweets in groups 1 and 2 using MapReduce and rmr. I ran:

library(rmr2)
library(tm)
library(topicmodels)

testdf.dfs=to.dfs(testdf)

corp.red=function(ind,text) {
  tweets=list(text)
  corp = Corpus(VectorSource(tweets))
  corp = tm_map(corp, tolower)
  corp = tm_map(corp, stripWhitespace)
  corp = tm_map(corp, removePunctuation)
  corp = tm_map(corp, removeNumbers)
  corp = tm_map(corp, removeWords, stopwords('english'))
  corp.DTM = DocumentTermMatrix(corp)
  topic_model = LDA(corp.DTM,k=2)
  keyval(ind,topic_model)
}

topics.bigdata=mapreduce(input=testdf.dfs,
                         map=function(k,v) keyval(v$topic,v$text),
                         reduce=corp.red)
tweet_topics = from.dfs(topics.bigdata)
n_results = 2
terms = lapply(tweet_topics, function(kv) terms(values(kv), n_results))

print(terms)

I got the error:

13/06/11 15:54:50 ERROR streaming.StreamJob: Job not successful. Error: NA
13/06/11 15:54:50 INFO streaming.StreamJob: killJob...
Streaming Command Failed!
Error in mr(map = map, reduce = reduce, combine = combine, in.folder = if (is.list(input)) { :
  hadoop streaming failed with error code 1

And from stderror logs:

Warning in is.na <http://is.na>(x) :
  is.na <http://is.na>() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
Error in LDA(corp.DTM, k = 2) :
Each row of the input matrix needs to contain at least one non-zero entry
Calls: <Anonymous> ... evalVis -> withVisible -> eval -> eval -> reduce -> LDA
Execution halted
java.lang.RuntimeException: PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(): subprocess failed with code 1
	at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(PipeMapRed.java:365)
	at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeMapRed.mapRedFinished(PipeMapRed.java:579)
	at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeReducer.close(PipeReducer.java:137)
	at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.ReduceTask.runOldReducer(ReduceTask.java:509)
	at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.ReduceTask.run(ReduceTask.java:447)
	at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child$4.run(Child.java:270)
	at java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged(Native Method)
	at javax.security.auth.Subject.doAs(Subject.java:396)
	at org.apache.hadoop.security.UserGroupInformation.doAs(UserGroupInformation.java:1127)
	at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child.main(Child.java:264)

The LDA function requires a Document Term Matrix as an input argument. Again, it could be that this not an rmr2 question, but I still wanted to check here. Even if not fixed, any comments towards optimizing and making my code more efficient are welcome.

Thanks in advance!!

messages.subject: rhbase 1.2.0 and rhdfs 1.0.6 released
messages.body_plain:
rhdfs adds windows compatibility (when used with HDP for windows). rhbase has a new serialization option, "character", which is appropriate when cell contents are textual. This was previously and not so accurately named "raw". "raw" is now really raw, meaning cell contents are represented with raw vectors, no transformation occurs.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: [RHadoop:#798] Problems with the installation of RHadoop (java.io.IOException: Error opening job jar: loadtb)
messages.body_plain:
Try to set the shell variable HADOOP_STREAMING to the streaming jar. If you don't specify it, rmr2 looks for $HADOOP_HOME/contrib/streaming/hadoop-streaming*.jar That may or may not be correct for all distributions and is considered the legacy way to configure rmr2. Setting the pair HADOOP_CMD and HADOOP_STREAMING has generalized better to a variety of distros. The error message could be more intuitive,  I agree. Please create an issue on the rmr2 github issue tracker and I will look into that.

Antonio

messages.subject: Re: Logistic Regression using rmr2 package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Souvik,
unfortunately these are just examples and are not supported like the documented API. I suspect that once you get the coefficients of the model it should be possible to build the model and call predict, but I don't have code to do that. I also suspect choosing {-1,1} vs {0,1} is pretty much equivalent but you need to stay consistent with the math, because it corresponds to picking a different link function (see Family in R), so the derivatives are going to be a little different.

Antonio
